sections.h2: Where is Rankin County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Rankin County sits in central Mississippi on the Pearl River, next to Hinds County and the Jackson area. The Mississippi Encyclopedia says it was founded in 1828 from part of Hinds County and named for political figure Christopher Rankin. Brandon is the county seat.

The county's own demographics page lists nine communities: Brandon, Florence, Flowood, Pearl, Pelahatchie, Puckett, Richland, Sandhill and Star. Wikipedia reports a 2020 census population of 157,031, the fourth-most populous county in Mississippi, with Pearl as the largest city.

sections.h2: How did Rankin County change from farmland to suburbs?
sections.html:
Rankin County moved from a mostly agricultural economy to a heavily populated suburban county over the twentieth century. The Mississippi Encyclopedia describes the recent shift away from agriculture and notes that in 1960 farmers made up just 13 percent of the workforce, with nearly a quarter of workers in industry, mainly furniture and timber.

It also names two long-standing institutions in the county: the Piney Woods Country Life School, started in 1909, and the Mississippi State Hospital at Whitfield. The state moved the hospital there from Jackson in the 1920s, and the town took the name Whitfield for Rankin native Henry Whitfield, governor from 1924 to 1926.

The same source notes that the county sits next to Hinds County and its urban center of Jackson, and that Rankin had no urban population of its own in the early twentieth century. Its population reached almost 44,000 in 1970 and topped 69,000 a decade later, which is the growth that turned small towns such as Brandon, Pearl and Flowood into the communities listed above.

sections.h2: Which Rankin County offices handle property tax and land records?
sections.html:
Three offices matter: the Tax Assessor, the Tax Collector and the Chancery Clerk. Our main page covers the Tax Collector's hours and online payment. These are the other two, taken from the county website.

OfficeRoleLocation and contact
Tax AssessorValues property, takes homestead applicationsCourthouse Annex, 211 E Government St, Brandon; (601) 825-1470
Chancery ClerkLand records, recording, tax sale redemptionCourthouse Annex Suite D, 211 E Government St; mail to P O Box 700, Brandon 39043; (601) 825-1469; Mon to Fri 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The Chancery Clerk's office has separate pages for e-recording, recording requirements and delinquent taxes. Under state law the clerk is the custodian of land records and also administers the annual county tax sale, as the Department of Revenue explains.

sections.h2: How does homestead exemption work in Rankin County?
sections.html:
You file for homestead exemption with the Rankin County Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1, and the first filing has to be made in person. According to the county's Filings and Exemptions page, the benefit renews automatically each year after that unless your filing status changes.

A new application is needed after these changes:

  • Marriage, divorce, separation, or the death of a spouse or joint owner.
  • A change in ownership, use or occupancy.
  • Acquiring new property or a change in the property description.
  • Turning sixty-five or becoming 100% disabled for the first time.

The county warns that failing to tell the Tax Assessor about a change in homestead status may bring a fine of up to $5,000, two years in prison, or both. An owner who is 65 or older, or 100% disabled, is generally exempt on 160 acres or about $75,000 of appraised value, whichever limit is reached first. Anything over that is taxed.

If you sell a house that carries a homestead exemption, the county asks owners to report changes in ownership, use or occupancy to the Tax Assessor.

sections.h2: How are Rankin County taxes figured and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Rankin County bills follow the state formula, which is true value times assessment ratio times the combined millage for your county, school district and, if you live in a city, that city. The state classes owner-occupied single-family homes at 10% of true value and other real property at 15%, per the Department of Revenue FAQ.

Taxes are due by February 1, and unpaid real property tax can lead to a sale at the county tax auction. The sale falls on the first Monday in April or the last Monday in August depending on the county, and Rankin's own page on the topic is the place to confirm it.

After a tax sale, the Chancery Clerk's Land Redemption page offers an online search for delinquent tax amounts and redemption information. Credit card payments carry a 2.5% convenience charge and debit transactions a $2.25 flat fee. Questions go to the Chancery Clerk's office at 601-825-1469.

A seller who is behind should look up the amount first. The title company will ask for it before closing.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Rankin County?
sections.html:
Rankin is on the list of counties that collect the $1 archive fee, so a deed with up to five pages runs $26 plus $1 for each extra page. That comes from the statewide schedule under Miss. Code 25-7-9, effective January 1, 2020, posted by the Harrison County Chancery Clerk from the Mississippi Chancery Clerk's Association.

The recorder can add $10 for a document that does not meet the format rules in Miss. Code 89-5-24. Fees may change, so call the Rankin Chancery Clerk before sending a check. Our Mississippi quitclaim deed guide explains the format and recording rules.

sections.h2: What do Rankin County sellers usually deal with?
sections.html:
Sellers in Rankin County most often deal with taxes that are late, a house that came through an estate, or a place that needs work before a buyer's lender will approve it. Pulling the facts together early makes each of these easier.

  • Get the current tax statement from the Tax Collector and check whether homestead exemption is on file with the Tax Assessor.
  • Ask the Chancery Clerk to confirm the deed of record and any tax sale or redemption history.
  • For an inherited house, find out whether the estate is open, and see our probate guide.
  • Check the county website for posted notices before you plan yard clearing. It currently shows a burn ban effective October 15, 2026.

We buy Rankin County houses as-is and reply with a written offer. The guide above does not promise a price, and we suggest confirming any tax figure with the county offices.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Rankin County?
faqs.a: Property tax is paid to the Rankin County Tax Collector. The Tax Assessor handles value and homestead exemption, and the Chancery Clerk handles land records and tax sale redemption.

faqs.q: When do I file for homestead exemption in Rankin County?
faqs.a: Between January 1 and April 1, in person at the Tax Assessor's office the first time. After that it renews automatically unless something changes, such as ownership, marriage or divorce.

faqs.q: Is there a tax sale in Rankin County?
faqs.a: Mississippi counties hold annual tax sales for delinquent real property tax, on the first Monday in April or the last Monday in August. The Rankin Chancery Clerk publishes delinquent tax and redemption information online.

faqs.q: How do I check redemption amounts after a Rankin County tax sale?
faqs.a: Use the Land Redemption page on the Rankin County website, or call the Chancery Clerk at 601-825-1469. Credit card payments carry a 2.5% convenience charge.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Rankin County with tax due?
faqs.a: Yes. The amount owed is confirmed through the Tax Collector or Chancery Clerk before closing, and a cash buyer can purchase the house as-is. Check the amount and any sale history first.
